title: Ulun Danu Beratan Temple.jpg
author: Yessykharisma
description:
Pura Ulun Danu Bratan, or the Ulun Danu Temple, is located on Lake Bratan, on the territory of the village of Candikuning, near Bedugul, Baturiti district, Tabanan Regency, Bali, Indonesia. It is 30 miles (48 km) north of the city of Denpasar or 12 miles (20 km) south of Singaraja city. 
It is the second most important temple in Bali after the Pura Besakih, and one of Bali’s most visited tourist destinations.
The Ulun Danu Temple is paramount amongst all water temples that govern the subak irrigation system, that draw water from Lake Batur. The subak system, unique to Bali, was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage. It comprises not only the technical elements of terraces cultivation, but also the social and religious unity in Bali known locally at ‘Tri Hata Karana’. 
It is believed by the Balinese that the temple embodies the meaning of universal balance. In Balinese Rwa Bhineda (the balance of two opposites), the Ulun Danu temple is regarded as Pradana (feminine) while the Besakih Temple is Purusha (masculine). Besakih Temple is where the Balinese worship their almighty for strength for the soul of the people in order to achieve spiritual satisfaction. At Ulun Danu Temple, prayers are conducted to strengthen prosperity.
Rebuilt in 1926, the Ulun Danu Temple is dedicated to the goddess of lakes and rivers, Dewi Batari Ulun Danu. ‘Ulun Danu’ means ‘above the lake’.

Lake Bratan alone stands as a significant part of the Ulun Danu Temple.
location: Templo Ulun Danu Beratan, Bali, Indonésia
